message: The Email has no lang, so screen readers guess its language
The Email has no previewText, so inboxes show its first words after the subject
fix: give the Email a previewText of 30 characters or more

message: The image's alt, "logo", says nothing about what it shows
fix: say what the image shows ("Tarn's logo", "A blue bowl"), or leave alt empty if it's only decoration

message: This text is 2.64:1 against its background (#9aa0a6 on #ffffff): body text needs 4.5:1
fix: darken the text or lighten the background (or the reverse) until it reaches the ratio
make it 14px or larger, on phones at least (style.mobile.fontSize)

message: The Button says "Click here": a screen reader lists links by their words alone
fix: say where it goes ("Confirm your email"), or give it an aria-label

message: "482913" is read as one number, not as digits: write it as "482 913"
fix: Group the digits with spaces (482 913) so they're read one by one, and the reader can keep their place.

message: Its line height is 1.30 times the font size: make it 1.5
fix: Set lineHeight to 1.5 for body text.

message: This button is about 80×22 px: a tap target needs at least 24×24 px, and 44 px tall is better on a phone
fix: Give the button padding so it's at least 24 px tall and wide; 44 px is better on phones.

message: These social icons are 18 px: a tap target needs at least 24×24 px
fix: Give the button padding so it's at least 24 px tall and wide; 44 px is better on phones.

message: 1 table has no header cells and no role="presentation": a screen reader announces it as a data table
fix: Use Rows and Columns (Hyper Elements marks their tables role="presentation"), or add the role to the table in an Html block.

message: The email has no headings: a screen reader user can't jump to what matters
fix: Start with one level-1 Heading saying what the email is about, and use Headings for its sections.
